title: NATIVE ON build, Agent 5 uploads, user-window version (task #15): u0 batch-2 defaults, u1 legacy upload CPU paths, u2 texture staging pool; 5 runs each with 60 s windows, load phase scored by bench/agent5/load_phase.py. Title/attract loop from boot, no input needed
notes: USER-WINDOW VERSION (task #15, Agent 1 03:07): the 45-minute cut of bench/agent5/matrix-native-uploads.json. Same bin, cvars, env and 60 s window floor. Only the three timing arms, 5 runs each, with a 60 s scored window instead of 120 s. Every run is a fresh process and pays the first-use uploads in its first minute, so this gives 5 load-phase samples per arm (smallest exact p at 5v5: 0.008). The s0/s1/s2 diagnostic rows stay in matrix-native-uploads.json (final, sha256 15BB7822..., unchanged); Agent 8 runs them in its own slot with -Only s0,s1,s2, and they need no user window.

BIN DIR: build/agent2/native3-bin (Agent 2, staged 02:45:57; exe sha256 7F7F8586D219465C, MANIFEST.txt B50FE8D4A16565DA, native GPU fingerprint 8f849b69907d4006). It is the S3 snapshot with NATIVE_GPU=ON. Batch 2 is in (all three batch-2 strings are in the exe, and MANIFEST.txt lists the 8 Agent 5 files) and so is fix-a, so it boots with the settings frontend on (Agent 8 boot PASS, build/agent8/runs/0256-native3). Do not swap in an older native bin: native-bin (S1) has neither env switch, so u1/u2 would equal u0, and native-bin and native2-bin throw at startup with the frontend on.

WINDOW (Agent 1's 60 s floor): settle_s 50 + warmup_s 10 from the first-frame signal, so the scored window covers 60-120 s after the first frame (cold run: 60-90 s). min_window_after_ff_s is set to 60 explicitly (the runner default), so no warm-up is raised. On the frame clock (interval_ms summed over the rows before frames.window.first_row), Agent 8's S3 runs started their windows 0.2-0.4 s after settle + warm-up, so expect about 60.3 s after the real first frame. The light-to-heavy title switch comes 30.6-32.6 s after the first frame (window 3 and S3 runs), so it falls in the settle, about 28 s before the window. load_phase.py prints each run's window start (ff->win s) and flags win<60s if one starts early. -Quick (settle 5 s) is functional only and never scored.

UNCAPPED (SG rule): every arm passes native_fps_limit=0 and framerate_limit=0. The runner adds the standard flags itself (common.ps1:99-100: --native_settings_load=false --discord_rpc=false --audio_mute=true --pause_when_unfocused=false), so they are not repeated here. No arm sets native_settings_frontend=false: the build must boot with the settings frontend on. With the frontend on, the cap is LEGO_NATIVE_FPS_LIMIT if that env is set, else the native_fps_limit cvar (settings_snapshot.cpp:64-65; the frontend only reads the env). No arm sets that env, so the cvar uncaps it. Check: the native_fps_limit_cvar column of native-frames.csv (the cap in force) must be 0 in every row; load_phase.py flags capN otherwise. Agent 8's native3 boot run without these cvars (build/agent8/runs/0256-native3) shows 240 in all 13642 rows.

SCORING 1, the scored window (the runner, as usual): mean fps, p50, p99, over_33ms, over_100ms, max_ms and CPU over 60-120 s after the first frame. It measures the steady-state upload cost of the title/attract loop: textures streamed in after boot (u1: scalar untile and byte swap) and per-upload staging buffer creation (u2). Expect a tie: on the quiet window-3 n0 runs every frame over 33 ms came in the first 1.4 s and no frame after 5 s took more than 25 ms. A tie is a valid result. Report runs with Agent 8's light-phase flag separately.

SCORING 2, the load phase (no extra runs): after the matrix, run: python bench/agent5/load_phase.py <matrix output dir> --ref u0 --md <matrix output dir>/load-phase.md --csv <matrix output dir>/load-phase.csv --json <matrix output dir>/load-phase.json. From row 0 of each run's native-frames.csv (perf.csv as a cross-check) it scores the first 60 s after the first frame: frames over 33/50/100 ms, hitch ms, max frame, p99, launch to first frame (game.log 'Native presentation: frame=0'), first frame to title (the draw-count switch), title max (max frame from 2 s before to 5 s after the switch) and o20 5s+ (frames over 20 ms after 5 s, a busy-machine check). It compares u1 and u2 with u0 (difference of medians and an exact permutation p) and leaves out cold, light-phase, failed and short runs. Stdlib Python, one thread, read-only on the run dirs. These are first-use costs, not timing results.

EXPECT, from the 5 quiet window-3 n0 runs (r1-r4 and the cold run; native2-bin, frontend off; native3-bin with the frontend on may shift the absolute values): u0: o33 3-4, o50 0-2, o100 0-1, max 50-154 ms, all in the startup burst in the first 1.4 s (per-run PSO compiles and first uploads); p99 10-12 ms; title max 13-16 ms; first frame to title 30.6-31.2 s; launch to first frame 12.7-17.2 s. u1 (old CPU paths, same output bytes): a bigger startup burst and maybe a spike at the title switch. At 5v5 the load phase separates it from u0 only if the effect is large and consistent, for example 2 or more extra frames over 33 ms, or a title max above 20 ms, in every run. First frame to title should not move: it follows a timed intro. Scored window: a tie. u2 (staging pool): a tie with u0 on every load-phase and window metric, because saving one createBuffer per staged upload is far below the run-to-run noise. Its checks are functional: the pool lines, commit, no corruption, and allocate-map-stage in Agent 8's s2-vs-s0 diagnostic.
u2 must log 'Native texture staging pool: enabled, 64 MB idle budget' once and 'Native texture staging pool: hits=... misses=...' every 256 staged uploads. u0 and u1 must log neither.
Memory: compare commit / peak commit between u2 and u0 (the pool keeps <= 64 MB idle, and pooled capacities round up to a power of two).

CORRUPTION (nobody watches the screen): a staging buffer reused before its copy retired would draw wrong textures without any log line, so only a person or a screenshot can rule it out. Log checks per run (game*.log); each count must be 0, or the same in u2 as in u0: 'texture upload allocation failed' (textures.cpp:2446), 'texture allocation failed' (textures.cpp:1107), 'failed to allocate' (buffers.cpp:467), 'cannot wait for submission after device removal' (device.cpp:657), and 'Native texture binding:' / 'Native texture binding totals:' (draw.cpp:928/932, with unavailable, upload_rejected and view_lost counts). Baseline: 0 [error] lines and 31 non-INSTALL [warning] lines in both window-3 0030-n0-r1 and build/agent8/runs/0256-native3. If u2 differs from u0 in any of them, stop the arm and tell Agent 5.
No LEGO_NATIVE_TIMING, LEGO_NATIVE_SLOW_OPERATIONS or debug layer in these arms.

QUIET MACHINE: the load phase is very sensitive to background load. Busy runs (verify3b, and S3 n1-n3 on the hidden desktop) had 27-88 frames over 33 ms and 112-295 frames over 20 ms after 5 s, and the 0256 boot run (94% system busy) had 44 over 20 ms, against 3-4 and 0-2 on the quiet window-3 runs. Run it on an idle machine; load_phase.py flags a run with more than 20 frames over 20 ms after 5 s as noisy. sys_csv is on, as in window 4's matrix: every run logs sys.csv and sys.json (1 s), so input, foreground loss, screensaver and power changes get flagged.

SIZE: 16 runs, 1 unscored cold u0 and then 5 rounds of u0, u1 and u2. -PlanOnly (runner of 02:53): about 41 min. Expect 41-42 min on a quiet machine, and at most about 44 min if every boot is slow. On the S3 runs, close + post-processing + cooldown took 21 s against the planned 20 s, and launch to window start took launch-to-first-frame (13-21 s, against the planner's 12 s) + settle + warm-up + 0.3-0.5 s. If the window is shorter, -Repeats 4 is 13 runs, about 33 min (smallest p 0.029). Agent 1 (03:02): not window 4.

arms.note: Agent 5 u0: batch-2 defaults (SIMD untile, no staging zero-fill, SIMD byte swap, no staging pool)
Agent 5 u1: old upload CPU paths. Expect slower uploads than u0 (more or longer upload spikes)
Agent 5 u2: pooled texture staging buffers (64 MB idle). Check the pool log lines, commit, and no corruption
